column1: # Gaps of the 'svcparam' block that are no longer gaps, keyed to the same
# 'killed' means a mutation taken from this sweep's output now fails a test.
# 'equivalent' means the mutation is real and the program is the same either way.
# 'superseded' means the line the verdict belongs to was replaced by a fix.

column6: Value.Length > 0 in ToString(), which is the debugging text and not the presentation format. The mutant calls EscapeValue on an empty value, which returns an empty string - what the other branch wrote

keyName.Length > 3 in the test for the unknown-key form. A name of three characters reaches the line only if TryParseKey knows it, and the one it knows is "ech", which does not start with "key"; "key" itself has no number and was passed over above. So the next clause is false either way

Position >= Text.Length inside a quoted value, which is a quote that is never closed. The mutant reads one character past the end instead, and the IndexOutOfRangeException ends the read where the FormatException did: SVCB.TryParseFromJSON and HTTPS.TryParseFromJSON catch every exception, and the zone-file reader reaches them through those. The record is refused either way and the error it reports is the same
Position + 1 >= Text.Length, a backslash at the end of the text. As at 243: the mutant indexes past the end, and the exception it throws is caught where the FormatException was

the first || of the three-digit test. The mutant drops the check of the second digit wherever the third is in reach, and the next statement is Int32.Parse over all three - which throws a FormatException of its own for a digit, a non-digit and a digit, since the first and the last are checked. The blank after two digits, which Int32.Parse would forgive, is the third character's case and line 309's
Position + 3 >= Text.Length, a decimal escape cut short by the end of the text. As at 243: the mutant indexes past the end, and the exception it throws is caught where the FormatException was

!HasValue || Value.Length == 0 in ValueList. The mutant lets an "=" with nothing after it through, and the loop below then finds no item at all and throws at its own end: "the list has an empty item". The same refusal from a line further down
i + 1 >= Value.Length, a backslash at the end of a list. As at 243: the mutant indexes past the end, and the exception it throws is caught where the FormatException was
